children.text: A home within the neighbourhood

This concept explores adapting a typical Birmingham house around the everyday needs of children and their carers. The emphasis is on retaining a familiar residential character, with an ordinary entrance, restrained landscaping and a welcoming arrival.
Making the existing layout work

The design brief considers a shared kitchen and dining space, a separate lounge and a quieter room for study or time away from communal activity. Private bedrooms and practical staff facilities would be developed around an agreed care model and a measured survey.
Testing the proposal

Before progressing a real property, the work would need to establish the proposed occupancy, staffing arrangements, parking, outdoor space and relationship with neighbours. The appropriate planning route would be assessed against the actual use and site circumstances.

children.text: More room for everyday life

The concept considers an existing detached house with a modest single-storey rear addition. Its pitched roof and brickwork are intended to sit comfortably alongside the original building while creating a generous shared room at garden level.
A usable garden connection

The design focus is on a simple relationship between indoor living, a sheltered terrace and an enclosed garden. A separate quiet room would allow different activities to take place without making the home feel institutional.
Developing a site-specific design

A real scheme would require a measured survey, an operator brief and an assessment of neighbouring windows, boundaries, access and parking. Extension dimensions, safeguarding measures and the approval strategy would follow that work.

This interior concept explores how an existing house could offer a calm, comfortable setting for children and carers. Soft colours, familiar furniture and natural daylight provide the starting point for a welcoming shared living room.
Choice and privacy

The wider remodelling brief would balance communal spaces with opportunities for quiet activity and privacy. Storage, acoustic separation and discreet staff facilities would be considered alongside circulation and the practical routines of the home.
